book.title: Focus: The Hidden Driver of Excellence
book.author: Daniel Goleman

confidence_note: Verified from excerpts/summaries: attention strength is limited but trainable; neuroplasticity for a practiced skill needs attention; returning from a wandering mind matters for brain wiring; mind-wandering has costs and uses; research on digital games. Old-text specifics (neurobiologist friend dialogue, Merzenich owl monkeys, Polley 2006, Lazar and Hölzel eight-week study) could not be tied to the book and were dropped. Book text not read.
facts: Goleman: attention strength is limited but can be improved by training, like a muscle.
Neuroplasticity, the strengthening of old circuits and building of new ones for a practiced skill, requires paying attention; practice with attention elsewhere does not rewire the relevant circuits.
Training works by building connections between neurons.
Mindfulness means noticing thoughts, letting them go and directing attention back; bringing the mind back has profound significance for the wiring of the brain.
Mind-wandering is the default mode, supports self-reflection and problem-solving but raises errors and accidents, lowers comprehension and can become rumination; it cannot be forced.
Research suggests digital games can improve visual attention, object tracking, processing speed, task switching and memory capacity.
Goleman discusses meditation and digital games as training.
scene_details: noticing the mind has wandered and bringing it back
tension: Practicing a skill with attention elsewhere does not change the circuits for it.
opening_idea: The training moment is the return from wandering.

lessons.idea: Practice only counts when attention is on it.
lessons.anchor: Neuroplasticity requires paying attention; practice with attention elsewhere does not rewire.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A learner practicing guitar scales while watching TV.

reflect_final: During which task this week did your attention stay put for a full stretch, and what happened to it when your phone buzzed?

use_cases.move: Put phones away during practice so attention is on the skill.
Ask them to notice when they drift and come back.
Each time you notice drifting, count it as a return.

pocket_idea: Each time you notice your mind drifting and bring it back is the training.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Practice with attention elsewhere does not rewire the brain.
